source: core::ares_core::VulnerabilityCategory (Rust, core/crates/ares-core/src/lib.rs:51-73) -- 21 variants, verified by direct read, not by count in a prior summary
notes: Two independently-evolved vocabularies -- 21 Rust variants vs. 34 VULN_CATALOG ids -- with 8 verbatim string matches: type-cosplay, arbitrary-cpi, account-data-matching, pda-privileges, reentrancy-risk, missing-revalidation, fuzzing-crash, state-transition-gap (the last 5 added by ENG-2, which also added matching catalog entries for categories that previously had none). Everything else below is a human judgement call, not a formal equivalence. Read this before quoting any precision/recall number derived through this mapping.

duplicate-mutable-accounts (Rust, plural) vs duplicate-mutable-account (Python/TS, singular) look like a typo-level mismatch but are two independently spelled strings in two independently maintained files. Without this explicit mapping entry, score_detections.py's default exact-match category key would silently score every true positive on this category as a miss.

close-account and revival-attack (two distinct Rust variants) both plausibly map to the single VULN_CATALOG id account-close-revival -- a many-to-one collapse. This means the Rust vocabulary is finer-grained here, not that it is redundant; both still map, since the ground truth only ever asks for account-close-revival.
signer-authorization and missing-signer (two distinct Rust enum variants, lib.rs:54,68) both plausibly mean 'missing signer check' in practice -- both map to missing-signer-check.

account-reloading, re-initialization, and revival-attack are handled distinctly in Rust's from_str_checked/Display (lib.rs:106-125) even though they alias together in Rust's own parser in one spot -- this mapping keeps them as three separate Rust source categories mapped to three separate VULN_CATALOG ids (missing-reload-after-cpi, account-reinitialization, account-close-revival) since that is the finer distinction the catalog actually supports; only close-account collapses together with revival-attack per the note above.

fuzzing-crash and invariant-violation are engine-internal categories that (per this repo's own scope) can only be produced by a --fuzz run. The scan-only pass this mapping was built for (--fuzz false) should never emit fuzzing-crash in practice; ENG-2 gave it a real catalog id (its own name, exact match) so it now scores correctly whenever a --fuzz pass does emit it. invariant-violation is mapped to business-logic-error as a coarse stretch since it can also surface from cross-instruction static analysis, not only fuzzing.

state-transition-gap (added by ENG-2) is emitted by ares-mapper's cross_analysis::find_state_transition_gaps but, before ENG-2, had no Rust enum variant at all -- scan.rs's from_str_checked(...).unwrap_or(InvariantViolation) silently mislabeled every one of these findings as invariant-violation. Both the Rust variant and this mapping entry are new; it maps to itself, exact confidence.

Rust categories with no defensible VULN_CATALOG equivalent are mapped to null and scored downstream as the literal string 'other' -- by design. Forcing a bad mapping to inflate recall/precision would defeat the point of measuring anything. An unmapped category genuinely has no ground-truth correspondence to be credited against.

generic is Rust's catch-all/fallback category (lib.rs:72) with no defensible single VULN_CATALOG equivalent -- mapped to null/other, same as the other unmapped entries, not given special treatment. ENG-2 deliberately excluded it from the catalog rather than forcing a misleading CWE onto plumbing that isn't a real vulnerability class.

'confidence' field below is this mapping's own quality flag on the TRANSLATION (exact | semantic | semantic-plural-mismatch | coarse-stretch | not-applicable-static-scan | unmapped), unrelated to Finding.confidence (a float on the Rust side) or the CSV 'confidence' column (low/medium/high bucket of that float) -- three different things named similarly across three different files; do not conflate them when reading this file or the converter script.
